sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant/accused,
relating to FIR/Crime No.34/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Choti Gwaltoli, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC.
2 .
Prosecution story, in brief is that there was friendship between the prosecutrix and the applicant since 02 years before the incident.
On 09.04.2022, the applicant had taken the prosecutrix to Hotel Shree Mahalakshmi Palace at 06:00 PM, on the occasion of his birthday.

There the applicant made Nitin vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90096826/
1 the prosecutrix to consume beer and consequently, he raped the prosecutrix while she was intoxicated.

sentences.text: After 2 - 3 days, he had called her to develop physical relation, but the prosecutrix had denied for the same.
Then the applicant had threatened her for making her obscene videos go viral.
He had given her life threat as well.
Since then he has repeated the offence on several occasions.

The matter was reported by the prosecutrix on 10.02.2024.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix is major and a married lady.

It is also submitted that in the year 2023, husband of the prosecutrix had filed a divorce petition, HM Case No.726/2023, wherein her husband had taken ground of illicit relationship coupled with other grounds, between prosecutrix and applicant.
It is also submitted that the FIR was lodged with unexplained delay of around 2 years.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix was a consenting party for sexual intercourse but later on due to some disputes, she lodged a false FIR against the applicant.
Applicant is in custody since 11.02.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
No further custodial interrogation is required.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of the application.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the allegations made against the applicant, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant - Nitin shall be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Nitin vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90096826/
